title: SignRep supplementary material

explicit_limit: Dataset identity and pretraining overlap must not be inferred from similar folder names
what_is_already_done: Validation-selected checkpoint and sign-prior masking already specified

title: SHuBERT: Self-Supervised Sign Language Representation Learning via Multi-Stream Cluster Prediction
relevant_sections: 3.1-3.2;4.1-4.4; encoder Appendix B details still pending

explicit_limit: Pretraining removes every other frame; native public raw-video scripts retain input FPS; downstream recipe TODO. Paper reports MS-ASL/YouTube-ASL test overlap, so no clean MS-ASL transfer claim.

remaining_question: Can independent grammar heads access cues a decoder ranking misses?

title: Targeted Linguistic Analysis of Sign Language Models with Minimal Translation Pairs

explicit_limit: Public demo checkpoint is not established as the paper checkpoint; MTP is external-only
what_is_already_done: Non-manual cue ablation and semantic minimal translation pairs already exist
remaining_question: Representation access versus readout utilization needs independent labels and fair controls

title: Lost in Expression: Diagnosing Systemic Challenges with Non-Manual Generalization in Sign Language Understanding Tasks
claim: Uni-Sign pose-only on SSL Isharah1000 compares signer-independent/unseen-sentence partitions and integrated gradients; authors distinguish feature attribution from faithful grammatical use
explicit_limit: Face keypoint selection omits eyebrow/eye-region detail; identification-cue and memorization interpretations are hypotheses, not causal isolation. Table2/prose SLT SI BLEU differ; do not use those numbers without resolution.
what_is_already_done: Signer/compositional partitions, integrated gradients, pipeline missingness and non-manual utilization diagnostics already exist
remaining_question: Gold functional tiers and temporal scope with frozen ASL encoders need direct evaluation; signer-disjoint classification alone is not a new task/method

title: SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval
claim: Pose articulator streams use standardized pooled saliency with Gumbel selection; gloss-supervised contrast plus dominant-only masking and context-to-clean latent prediction
explicit_limit: Saliency and input masking are already prior art; frozen grammar function/scope access is not established by cross-corpus lexical retrieval
what_is_already_done: Articulator saliency masking; cross-corpus retrieval; subtitle alignment already exist
remaining_question: Grammatical function and scope preservation beyond lexical identity is not established by retrieval

title: Phonological Representation Learning for Isolated Signs Improves Out-of-Vocabulary Generalization
version: version read from PDF pending registry
claim: Separate phonological pose streams and shared hand codebooks plus ASL-LEX-guided code assignments; same baseline-selected hyperparameters across variants
explicit_limit: Unseen-gloss Sem-Lex evaluation is not functional non-manual grammar scope; expert phonological labels are separate from sentence translations
what_is_already_done: Parameter disentanglement and phonological semi-supervision already exist
remaining_question: Do not claim VQ or generic linguistic disentanglement as a new mechanism

title: Grounding Sign Language Representation Learning in Phonology
claim: Dedicated handshape/location latent subspaces, multi-label focal loss plus auxiliary gloss; ASL pretraining and VGT cross-language neighborhood probing
explicit_limit: Explicit structured subspaces with lexical retention supervision already exist; evaluated parameters do not provide local ASL grammatical function/scope gold
what_is_already_done: Linguistically structured subspaces and nonparametric probing already exist
remaining_question: Function-versus-marker-versus-scope distinction needs gold and prior-art search

title: Phonological Perception of Sign Language Models
claim: Deaf-curated phonological minimal pairs compare penultimate latent intra-sign and inter-sign cosine similarities; re-trained ASL models exclude evaluation signs
explicit_limit: Reliable quantitative contrasts restricted to handshape/location/movement; nonmanual/orientation sparse. Ten sampled signer pairs feed t-tests; dependence/multiple testing need separate scrutiny. Supervised I3D/STGCN, not a modern SSL encoder evaluation.
what_is_already_done: Latent phonological sensitivity, minimal-pair controls and unseen-sign/domain comparisons already evaluated
remaining_question: Can modern SSL features preserve recorded functional core timing and support retention after a distinct encoder-side adaptation?

title: Sign Language Question Answering: A New Task, Benchmark, and Baseline for Sign Language Understanding
version: version read from PDF pending registry
claim: Gloss/text templates create SLQA on PHOENIX14T and CSL-Daily; question-conditioned temporal gating and channel modulation precede Conv1D/max pooling; staged recognition/translation transfer
explicit_limit: CSL-only interrogativity QA template is not a independently verified functional face-scope tier. Template-derived labels and fixed domains do not establish grammatical cue use. No direct comparison of localASL metrics.
what_is_already_done: Question-conditioned temporal feature retention, nonmanual interrogativity QA and in-domain multitask transfer already proposed
remaining_question: Does a distinct functional-scope representation repair add beyond generic conditioning/temporal pooling while retaining lexical information?

title: Scaling up sign spotting through sign language dictionaries
claim: Frozen16frameI3D trunk and trainable MLP use multiple-instance contrastive bags from dictionary variants, sparse mouthing annotations and subtitles to align isolated and continuous signing
explicit_limit: Spoken subtitle word occurrence does not guarantee sign occurrence; dictionary variants, fingerspelling and context-dependent words cause false positives. No expert ASL mapping inferred from this BSL work.
what_is_already_done: Isolated-to-continuous sign embeddings, weakly localized dictionary matching and multisupervision domain alignment already exist
remaining_question: Gold coarticulation transfer failure must be measured rather than presumed

title: Sign Spotting Disambiguation using Large Language Models
claim: I3D/handshape dictionary similarities and DTW-based intermediate/late fusion supply candidates; frozen LLM transition probabilities combine with visual scores in beam search
explicit_limit: BSL dictionary/segmentation quality and linguistic priors confound purely visual evidence; no reading claim for full experimental protocol or leakage audit. Do not treat text plausibility as verified sign occurrence.
what_is_already_done: Temporal dictionary matching, multimodal feature fusion and LLM context disambiguation already exist
remaining_question: Cannot claim dictionary DTW or LLM disambiguation as a new contribution

title: Towards Online Continuous Sign Language Recognition and Translation
claim: CTC-segmented pseudo sign dictionary and augmented windows train isolated recognition with foreground saliency and instance/gloss losses; sliding windows deduplicate and filter blanks; wait-k enables online translation
explicit_limit: Pseudo boundaries ambiguous; pose quality, context loss and gloss information loss limit scope. Continuous gloss annotations are not verified nonmanual functional intervals.
what_is_already_done: Foreground temporal supervision, context augmentations, online windows and frozen-feature fusion adapters already exist
remaining_question: An online processing claim must go beyond this prior

title: Drop-DTW: Aligning Common Signal Between Sequences While Dropping Outliers
claim: Drop-DTW permits interspersed dropped elements in monotonic alignment; percentile or learned costs and differentiable relaxation train representations and localize ordered steps
explicit_limit: Retains monotonicity and does not address arbitrary partially ordered signals; instructional-video localization is not direct ASL function evaluation. Drop costs require validation, not test tuning.
what_is_already_done: Differentiable alignment, background dropping and frozen-feature adaptation for interval localization already exist
remaining_question: A background/drop mechanism alone is not novel

title: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
claim: Content-free inputs estimate contextual answer priors; diagonal probability scaling or bias subtraction reduces prompt/example-order bias in few-shot language tasks
explicit_limit: Contextual bias correction differs from confidence calibration; reported generation calibration applies to first output token. Not evidence for ByT5 full-sequence candidate NLL calibration or grammatical cue use.
what_is_already_done: Data-free text-prior calibration and contextual bias controls already exist
remaining_question: Calibration can be a control but needs independent validation

title: A Pose-Based Pipeline for Annotation of Headshakes in Sign Language Corpora
claim: Yaw/velocity/acceleration with zero-crossing, bidirectional LSTM and CNN sliding windows; validation thresholds and annotation-assistance rationale
explicit_limit: DGS labels target grammatical negation rather than all headshakes; reported splits are not fully signer-independent; label mismatch and cross-language limits must remain explicit
what_is_already_done: Grammatical headshake annotation assistance and transfer already exist
remaining_question: Scope/function research must extend beyond detecting headshakes

title: Pose-Based Sign Language Spotting via an End-to-End Encoder Architecture
claim: Body/hand50keypoints per frame feed2DCNN and concatenated query/sentence Transformer withCLS/SEP/token-type embeddings; BCE predicts sign presence
explicit_limit: Binary presence, not interval localization; facial landmarks extracted but excluded from input. Paper80:20pair split does not prove signer/recording disjointness. Author first-task claim not adopted.
what_is_already_done: End-to-end visual-query sign-presence modeling with temporal cross-sequence interaction already exists
remaining_question: Can context-sensitive representation grounding improve verified interval localization and absence detection under disjoint query/target source groups?

what_is_already_done: Contrastive sign-text embeddings
